segments.text: Why does the bell curve show up everywhere?
segments.caption: Why does the bell curve show up everywhere?

segments.text: Even when the data isn't shaped like a bell?
segments.caption: Even when the data isn't shaped like a bell?

segments.text: The answer is the Central Limit Theorem.
segments.caption: The answer is the Central Limit Theorem.

segments.text: Here's what it says, in simple words.
segments.caption: Here's what it says, in simple words.

segments.text: Take many random samples, and find the average of each one.
segments.caption: Take many random samples, and find the average of each one.

segments.text: Those averages will form a bell curve, even if the original data isn't a bell.
segments.caption: Those averages will form a bell curve, even if the original data isn't a bell.

segments.text: You just need big enough samples, usually thirty or more.
segments.caption: You just need big enough samples, usually 30 or more.

segments.text: Let's see it with an example.
segments.caption: Let's see it with an example.

segments.text: Here are the salaries in a city.
segments.caption: Here are the salaries in a city.

segments.text: Most people earn a little, and a few earn a lot.
segments.caption: Most people earn a little, and a few earn a lot.

segments.text: So the data is skewed, not a bell.
segments.caption: So the data is skewed, not a bell.

segments.text: Step one: pick thirty people at random, and find their average salary.
segments.caption: Step 1: pick 30 people at random, and find their average salary.

segments.text: Step two: pick another thirty, and find their average.
segments.caption: Step 2: pick another 30, and find their average.

segments.text: Step three: repeat this again and again, and plot every average.
segments.caption: Step 3: repeat this again and again, and plot every average.

segments.text: Look! The averages form a bell curve.
segments.caption: Look! The averages form a bell curve.

segments.text: Why does this happen?
segments.caption: Why does this happen?

segments.text: In a random group of thirty, the few huge salaries get mixed with many ordinary ones.
segments.caption: In a random group of 30, the few huge salaries get mixed with many ordinary ones.

segments.text: So the extremes cancel out, and most averages land near the middle.
segments.caption: So the extremes cancel out, and most averages land near the middle.

segments.text: Two bonus facts.
segments.caption: Two bonus facts.

segments.text: The bell is centred on the true average of the whole city.
segments.caption: The bell is centred on the true average of the whole city.

segments.text: And bigger samples make it narrower, so your estimate gets more precise.
segments.caption: And bigger samples make it narrower, so your estimate gets more precise.

segments.text: So remember the Central Limit Theorem.
segments.caption: So remember the Central Limit Theorem.

segments.text: Many samples, one average each, and those averages make a bell curve, whatever the original shape.
segments.caption: Many samples, one average each, and those averages make a bell curve, whatever the original shape.

segments.text: That's why a survey of a few thousand people can describe a whole country.
segments.caption: That's why a survey of a few thousand people can describe a whole country.
